one_line: Regent-queen of Madurai who built roads and canals while steering her kingdom through Mughal–Maratha warfare.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, medium height, dignified and sturdy build with a poised, commanding stance.
appearance.face: Oval face with warm brown complexion, sharp nose, strong eyebrows, small beauty mark near the left cheekbone, and a calm but firm default expression that mixes empathy with strategic intensity.
appearance.hair: Black hair parted in the center, drawn back into a thick low bun at the nape, wrapped with a narrow gold-thread cloth band; a modest Madurai-style gold maang tikka at the parting and small gold jhumka earrings, no crown but clear royal refinement.
appearance.costume: She wears a late-17th-century Madurai Nayaka royal sari: a richly draped silk sari in deep maroon with broad mustard-gold borders woven in simple geometric motifs, pleats neatly tucked at the front and pallu brought from the back over the left shoulder to cover the torso fully; beneath is a short-sleeved choli in dark bottle green, largely hidden by the sari folds; a slim, engraved gold waist-belt (oddiyanam) holds the pleats; she has layered but not excessive jewellery—one medium-length gold chain, a single slightly longer chain with a small mango-shaped pendant, a few thin gold bangles on each wrist, and toe rings and anklets subtly visible above simple leather sandals suitable for travel along highways and inspection tours.
appearance.signature: A long rolled palm-leaf map tied with a red cotton ribbon, showing her road and irrigation projects, held confidently in her right hand like a planning tool rather than a weapon.

ref_desc: Rani Mangammal is a warm-brown skinned, late-middle-aged Madurai regent with an oval face, black hair in a low bun, maroon silk sari with mustard-gold borders, green choli, gold waist-belt and jewellery, holding a rolled palm-leaf map in her right hand.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Rani Mangammal: a late-middle-aged, dignified Madurai queen with a warm brown oval face, sharp nose, strong brows and a calm but firm expression, her black hair parted and pulled back into a thick low bun wrapped with a slim gold-thread band and adorned with a modest gold maang tikka and small gold jhumka earrings. She is fully clothed in an era-accurate late-17th-century Madurai Nayaka royal outfit: a deep maroon silk sari with broad mustard-gold borders in simple geometric motifs, neatly pleated at the front and draped so the pallu comes from the back over her left shoulder, covering her torso modestly, over a short-sleeved dark bottle green choli mostly hidden by the sari folds. A carved gold oddiyanam waist-belt secures the pleats, and she wears layered but restrained jewellery—a medium-length gold chain, a slightly longer chain with a small mango-shaped pendant, a few thin gold bangles on each wrist, subtle anklets and toe rings—and practical simple leather sandals that suggest she inspects roads and canals. In her right hand she confidently holds a long rolled palm-leaf map tied with a red cotton ribbon as her signature prop, symbolizing highway and irrigation planning. Show her standing in a neutral pose, front and three-quarter views if possible, emphasizing consistent face, hair, sari drape, colours, jewellery and the palm-leaf map, with clean lighting and no text or labels.
